reason: Science is long-term. Keep it out of day-to-day politics, let a board of people who know the field hold the money.
Researchers and the people using the work know what is needed. Local boards feel closer to us than a London committee.
Ministers answer to us at elections. A board nobody voted for worries me; tougher terms and a firm cap suit me better.
A ring-fenced board stops research being the first thing cut when the Treasury is short. It also has to publish costs.
